title: Global Run-On sequencing to measure nascent transcription in C. elegans
protocol: Mix 1.5 ml of cold nuclei extraction buffer and transfer to a pre-chilled stainless steel tissue grinder on ice.
Resuspend worms or embryos in the prepared buffer.
Apply 40 dounce strokes to lyse worms.
Check that the worms are lysed using a stereomicroscope; ensure no intact bodies or embryos remain.
Transfer the lysate to a pre-chilled 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 100×g for 4 min at 4°C.
Remove debris by centrifugation.
Transfer the supernatant to a new low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Carefully collect the supernatant without disturbing the debris pellet.
Repeat steps 4 and 5 until lysate is clear from debris.
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and wash nuclei with 1 mL NEB.
Wash nuclei by pipetting up and down several times using a wide-bore tip.
Gently pipette nuclei to preserve their integrity.
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C.
Repeat steps 7 and 8 three more times for a total of 4 washes with NEB.
Wash nuclei in 1 mL Freezing buffer NO-Glycerol.
Wash nuclei by pipetting up and down several times using a wide-bore tip.
Gently pipette nuclei to preserve their integrity.
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend nuclei in 100 μL Freezing buffer.
Prepare the NRO 2x mix according to the recipe provided.
Preheat the NRO 2x mix to 30°C before use.
Dispense 80 μL of the preheated NRO 2x mix into a low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 μL of Bio-11-UTP 10 mM to the NRO 2x mix (final concentration: 1 mM).
Gently mix the solution.
If running a negative NRO reaction, replace Bio-11-UTP with 0.5 μL UTP 100 mM and add 19.5 μL nuclease-free water instead.
Add 100 μL of lysed nuclei to the mixture.
Gently mix the reaction using a wide bore tip.
Incubate the reaction for 3 minutes at 30°C.
Transfer the tubes onto ice.
Add 50 μL of ice-cold nuclease-free water to the tubes.
Add 750 μL TRIzol LS reagent to stop the reaction.
Mix well to ensure thorough mixing.
Incubate nuclei in TRIzol for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Pause point: Nuclei in TRIzol can be stored at -80°C for up to a week.
Add 100 μL of 1-Bromo-3-chloropropane (BCP) to the mixture.
Vortex mix well by vortexing.
Incubate the sample at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 12,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous phase (upper phase) containing RNA to a new low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2 μL of GlycoBlue and mix well by vortexing for 5-10 seconds.
Add 500 μL of isopropanol and mix vigorously by vortexing for 10-15 seconds.
Incubate at room temperature (RT) for 15 minutes to precipitate the RNA.
Centrifuge at 12,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C to pellet the RNA.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of 75% Ethanol to the RNA pellet.
Centrifuge at 7,500×g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the RNA pellet.
Briefly centrifuge to collect all residual supernatant at the bottom of the tube.
Remove all residual ethanol using a p200 micropipette and ensure no residual ethanol is left in the tube.
Air dry the RNA pellet for 1-2 minutes.
Resuspend the RNA pellet from the previous step in 8 μL water.
Pause point: Store RNA at −80°C for up to a week if needed.
Add 2 μL of 5× reverse transcriptase buffer.
Mix the solution well by pipetting or vortexing.
Spin down the samples using a benchtop centrifuge.
Incubate the samples at 95°C for 7 minutes.
Transfer the samples to ice to block fragmentation immediately after incubation.
Add 50 μL of ice-cold nuclease-free water to the samples on ice and keep for at least 1 minute.
Resuspend the Dynabeads™ magnetic beads in the vial by vortexing for more than 30 seconds or tilting and rotating for 5 minutes.
Transfer 30 μL of Dynabeads™ magnetic beads per sample to a low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 30 μL of beads for samples of 1,000 to 40,000 adult worms or 40,000 to 300,000 embryos.
Mix with 1 mL of Binding & Washing Buffer 1× and resuspend by pipetting or gentle vortexing for 5–10 s.
Centrifuge the tube using a benchtop centrifuge briefly.
Place the tube on a magnet for 1 min until the solution appears clear, then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the magnetic beads in a volume of Binding & Washing Buffer 1× equal to the initial volume of beads taken from the vial by pipetting or gentle vortexing for 5–10 s.
Centrifuge the tube briefly.
Place the tube on a magnet for 1 min until the solution appears clear, then discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps 39-40 twice for a total of 3 washes.
Wash the beads twice in Solution A for 2 min using a volume equal to or larger than the initial bead volume.
Wash the beads once in Solution B using a volume equal to that used for Solution A.
Resuspend the beads in 60 μL per sample of 2× Binding & Washing Buffer.
Add 60 μL of washed beads from previous step to 60 μL of fragmented RNA from previous step.
Incubate for 30 min at 25°C with 1200 rpm agitation (15” ON 45” OFF) in a ThermoMixer.
Briefly spin the tubes using a benchtop centrifuge and place on a magnetic rack for 1 min or until the solution appears clear.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of High salt buffer.
Incubate on rotation for 5 min at 4°C.
Briefly spin the tubes using a benchtop centrifuge and place on a magnet for 1 min or until the solution appears clear.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of Medium salt buffer.
Incubate on rotation for 5 min at 4°C.
Briefly spin the tubes using a benchtop centrifuge and place on a magnet for 1 min or until the solution appears clear.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of Low salt buffer.
Incubate on rotation for 5 min at 4°C.
Briefly spin the tubes using a benchtop centrifuge and place on a magnet for 1 min or until the solution appears clear.
Remove the supernatant, add 1 mL TRI Reagent solution.
Resuspend RNA after TRIzol purification in 20 μL water.

Setup RNA 5′ phosphorylation reaction in 100 μL final volume by adding to the RNA from the previous step: 10 μL 10× Polynucleotide Kinase Buffer, 1 μL 100 mM ATP, 0.5 μL 40 U/μL RNase inhibitor, 2 μL 100 U/μL T4 Polynucleotide Kinase, and 66.5 μL water.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 30 min.
Add 200 μL of ice-cold nuclease-free water to the reaction mixture.
Keep the sample on ice.
Proceed to the next step.
Spin “5PRIME Phase Lock Gel™ – Heavy” tubes for 2 min at 12,000×g at room temperature (20°C–25˚C) to pellet the gel.
Add the solution from the previous step to a pre-spun Phase Lock tube.
Add 1 volume (300 μL) of Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl Alcohol and mix thoroughly by inverting 10–15 times.
Centrifuge at 12,000×g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Transfer the aqueous phase containing the RNA (upper phase) to a fresh low binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add 30 μL of 3 M sodium acetate and 2 μL of GlycoBlue and vortex for 5–10 s.
Add 900 μL ethanol and vortex vigorously for 10–15 s.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at −20°C to precipitate RNA.
Centrifuge to pellet the RNA at 12,000×g for 30 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of 75% Ethanol to the RNA pellet.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the RNA pellet.
Centrifuge at 12,000×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Air dry the RNA pellet for 1–2 minutes.
Resuspend the RNA in 5 μL of water.
Perform adapter ligation in a 20 μL final volume.
Add 1 μL of 10 μM 3SR adapter to the RNA from the previous step.
Add 2 μL of 10× Ligation Buffer.
Add 2 μL of “T4 RNA Ligase 2, truncated KQ”.
Add 10 μL of 50% PEG8000.
Mix well by pipetting up and down at least 20 times or vortexing.
Visually inspect that the solution is well mixed.
Incubate the reaction for 16 h at 16°C in a ThermoMixer equipped with a Thermo top.
Add 3 volumes (60 μL) of isopropanol to the ligation reaction from the previous step.
Add 1.8 volumes (36 μL) of Agencourt RNAClean XP beads.
Mix well by pipetting up and down at least 15 times or by gentle vortexing.
Incubate for 20 min on ice.
Briefly spin the tube.
Place the tube onto a magnetic tube rack for 5 min to separate the beads from the solution.
Slowly pipette the cleared solution from the tube and discard.
Dispense 200 μL of 75% ethanol into the tube on the magnetic rack, incubate for 30 s, and discard the ethanol.
Repeat the previous step for a total of 2 washes.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and briefly spin down residual ethanol using a benchtop centrifuge.
Place the tube onto a magnetic tube rack and remove residual ethanol.
Let the beads air dry for 5 min.
Add 61 μL water to elute purified RNA from the beads, manually resuspend the beads by pipetting up and down several times.
Expel the elution buffer down the side of the tube to ensure the entire bead mass comes into contact with the buffer.
Incubate for 30 s before proceeding to the next step.
Place the tubes onto a magnetic tube rack for 1 min to separate the beads from the solution.
Slowly collect 60 μL RNA solution and transfer to a fresh tube.
Heat purified RNA at 65°C for 5 min to denature secondary structures, place on ice for 1 min.
Perform a 2nd enrichment of biotinylated RNA molecules by repeating steps 45–54.
Resuspend RNA in 15 μL water after Trizol purification.
Mix the resuspended RNA with 1 μL of 5SR adapter, 2 μL of Ligation buffer 10×, and 2 μL of T4 RNA Ligase to a total volume of 20 μL.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 25°C for 2 hours.
Purify the RNA using Agencourt RNAClean XP beads as described in steps 73–84.
Heat purified RNA (60 μL) at 65°C for 5 minutes to denature secondary structures.
Place the heated RNA on ice for 1 minute.
Resuspend RNA after TRIzol purification in 11 μL of water.
Mix the resuspended RNA with 1 μL SR_RT primer, 1 μL dNTP mix, 4 μL SSIV Buffer 5×, 1 μL DTT, 1 μL RNase inhibitor, and 1 μL SuperScript IV reverse transcriptase to a final volume of 20 μL.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 50°C for 1 hour in a thermal cycler with the lid temperature set at 85°C.
Inactivate the reaction by heating the sample at 80°C for 10 minutes.
After reverse transcription, amplify libraries by PCR using a universal primer and a barcoded primer.
Perform a test PCR amplification of the libraries using ¼ of the reverse transcription reaction.
Determine the number of amplification cycles experimentally for each sample.
Minimize the number of PCR cycles to avoid overamplification.
Use different SR barcode primers for multiple samples if needed.
Add 90 μL AMPure XP beads to 50 μL PCR reaction.
Mix well by pipetting up and down at least 15 times or by gentle vortexing.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
Briefly spin using a benchtop centrifuge and place the tube onto a magnetic tube rack for 5 min.
Slowly pipette the cleared solution from the tube and discard.
While on the magnetic rack, dispense 200 μL of 75% ethanol into the tube.
Incubate for 30 s and remove the Ethanol.
Repeat the previous step for a total of 2 washes.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and briefly spin down residual ethanol using a benchtop centrifuge.
Place the tube onto a magnetic tube rack and remove residual ethanol.
Let the beads air dry for 5 min.
Elute purified DNA from the beads by adding 18 μL water.
Manually resuspend the beads by pipetting up and down several times.
Expel elution buffer down the side of the tube to ensure contact with the entire bead mass.
Incubate for 30 seconds before proceeding.
Place tubes onto a magnetic tube rack for 1 minute to separate beads from solution.
Slowly collect 17 μL of cleaned DNA libraries and transfer them to a fresh tube.
Add 1 μL of excess water at step 110 to prevent beads carryover.
Run 2 μL purified DNA libraries on an Agilent Tapestation instrument using High Sensitivity D1000 reagents.
Examine the result of the Tapestation run.
Determine the right PCR cycles for full-scale PCR amplification based on the results.
Adjust PCR cycles for each library to ensure they fall within the same range as upper and lower markers.
Check for over-amplification products (high molecular size) and reduce PCR cycles accordingly.

Set up a 50 μL full-scale PCR reaction by combining: 7 μL water, 15 μL reverse-transcribed cDNA library, 1.5 μL SR universal primer 10 μM, 1.5 μL SR barcode primer 10 μM, and 25 μL NEBNext® Ultra™ II Q5® Master Mix 2×.
Place the PCR reaction tube on a thermocycler with heated lid set to 105°C.
Perform PCR amplification using conditions specified in table:files/protocols_protocol_1210_13.csv.
Purify the PCR reaction by repeating steps 100–110 as described.
Run 2 μL of purified DNA libraries on an Agilent Tapestation instrument using High Sensitivity D1000 reagents according to manufacturer conditions.
Measure Qubit standard solutions before quantifying the DNA libraries.
Prepare 200 μL of working solution for each sample by diluting the Qubit® dsDNA HS Reagent 1:200 in Qubit® dsDNA HS Buffer.
Transfer 190 μL working solution and 10 μL standard solution into a new Qubit 0.5 mL tube (for both standards #1 and #2).
Transfer 198 μL of working solution and 2 μL of sample into a new Qubit 0.5 mL tube.
Mix well, briefly spin using a benchtop centrifuge.
Incubate the mixture for 2 min at RT.
Read sample concentration by selecting the dsDNA High Sensitivity as the assay type on the Qubit instrument.
Combine the average peak size with the concentration value to calculate the molarity of each library.
Pool all libraries that need to be sequenced together in an equimolar ratio.
Sequence pooled GRO-seq libraries using an Illumina Sequencing platform compatible with the TruSeq approach.
Use a NextSeq-500 instrument and the NextSeq 500/550 High Output Kit v2.5 (75 Cycles) for sequencing.
Generate 20–30 million reads per sample to ensure adequate coverage for both worms and embryos.
